title: Red Cell Ops — Neon Threat Matrix
description: A terminal-grade briefing surface for red-team leads and SOC analysts: monospace IP target tables, a glowing threat-level chip, and a left-rail status column that reads like a live ops console — not a slide.
philosophy: This template treats the slide as a system interface, not a presentation canvas. It borrows the dense information hierarchy of hardened dark-UI dashboards and Palantir-style ops tooling, refusing rounded-corner friendliness, stock imagery, or gradient washes that soften urgency. Every element earns its place through operational legibility — high-contrast monospace type, glow-edged threat callouts, and a structured grid that mirrors the mental model of the engineers in the room. It exists for audiences who read logs for a living and would distrust anything that looked designed to comfort.
goodFor: SOC incident summary and timeline walkthroughs
Penetration test scope and target-list reviews
Vulnerability disclosure briefings with risk-scored findings
avoidFor: External client-facing proposal or sales decks
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a classified ops terminal caught mid-initialization — the moment before a red-team lead briefs the room, the screen is already live, already watching. Compositional rhythm is hard-asymmetric: a thin vertical rail on the left pulses with system status indicators while the title dominates the remaining field with austere, glow-edged authority. Atmosphere is high-contrast and severe, borrowing from hardened dark-UI dashboards and cyber-range control interfaces — urgency without theatrics. Avoid anything editorial, ambient, or decorative; no soft glows, no abstract geometry, no visual metaphor that doesn't read as functional data.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; cols 1–2 form a left-rail status strip acting as a vertical signal bar — a thin glow-edged column containing a stacked operational status readout. Primary title occupies cols 3–10, vertically centered slightly above the mathematical midpoint to suggest an active display rather than a composed page. A horizontal rule line separates the title block from a subtitle/classification tag below it, with a threat-level chip anchored bottom-right. Outer margins are tight and utilitarian — roughly 4% bleed on sides — reinforcing the edge-hugging feel of a real console UI. Page metadata (date, operator ID placeholder) lives in the bottom-left gutter, monospace, subdued.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads as a hardened ops-console readout caught mid-incident — dense, purposeful, and stripped of any decorative intent. Compositional rhythm is tight-modular: left rail acts as a vertical status spine while the right field renders tabular threat data with glow-edge emphasis on critical-severity rows. Avoid rounded forms, gradient washes, or open whitespace that implies comfort; every gap should feel intentional, like whitespace in a config file. The overall affect is operational urgency expressed through discipline — a briefing surface that earns the trust of people who read logs for a living.

Main content occupies cols 3–12 and is structured as a dense monospace threat table or finding matrix, with a glowing threat-level chip anchored to the top-right corner of that zone. A scan-line rule bands the full width at the bottom, carrying a sequence counter and ISO-style timestamp label flush right. No softening outer margin — content bleeds close to all four edges to reinforce terminal-fill density.
